business.text: Intuitive Surgical makes the da Vinci surgical robot and the Ion lung biopsy system. Hospitals buy or lease the systems, then pay per procedure for instruments and service, which is most of the revenue.

guidance_diff.why: The last two 8-K Exhibit 99.1 press releases for this name have not been pulled from EDGAR, so there is no mechanical guidance diff. This is the free substitute for a transcript: it carries the guidance figures and none of the questions.
guidance_diff.caveat: Mechanical. Two press releases, sentences with a forward-looking word and a figure, matched on metric and period. It does not read tone, it cannot see a guide given without a number, and a filer that changes how it names a period between releases shows one lapsed and one introduced where a reader would see one reiterated. The verbatim sentence sits under every row so the machine's reading can be checked.

earnings_text.text: Q2 2026 (July 16, 2026): revenue $2.89 billion up 19%, procedures up 16%, 468 da Vinci systems placed vs 395, non-GAAP EPS $2.80 vs $2.19. Full year da Vinci procedure growth guided to 13.5% to 15.5%, gross margin 68 to 69% including a 1 point tariff hit. Shares fell 3.3% after hours despite the beat. Q1 2026 also beat with the same competition overhang.

read.headline: Intuitive's Q2 2026 beat on revenue, procedures and EPS, yet shares fell 3.3% after hours, and full-year gross margin is guided to 68 to 69% carrying a 1 point tariff hit.

guidance.what: Full year da Vinci procedure growth
guidance.detail: Guided to a range of 13.5% to 15.5%. The note gives no prior guidance range and does not say whether this was raised, cut, or maintained, so only the level is determinable. For context the note reports Q2 procedures up 16%, but it does not state that the guide represents a change to anything previously issued.
guidance.quote: Full year da Vinci procedure growth guided to 13.5% to 15.5%, gross margin 68 to 69% including a 1 point tariff hit.

guidance.detail: Guided to 68 to 69%, explicitly stated as including a 1 point tariff hit. No prior gross margin guide appears in the note, so whether this range moved is not determinable. The note separately reports FY2025 gross margin of 66.0% in its financials table, but that is an actual, not a prior guide.
guidance.quote: gross margin 68 to 69% including a 1 point tariff hit

tone.assessment: Management tone is not assessable from this note. The note contains no call commentary, no management quotes, no Q&A, and no characterization of how the quarter was presented. The only tone-adjacent observation available is arithmetic: the top of the full-year da Vinci procedure growth guide (15.5%) sits below the 16% procedure growth the quarter itself delivered. That is a comparison between a full-year range and a single quarter drawn by me from two numbers in the note, not a statement management made and not evidence of caution on their part.
tone.evidence: Full year da Vinci procedure growth guided to 13.5% to 15.5%, gross margin 68 to 69% including a 1 point tariff hit.

read.market_reaction: The note gives exactly one reaction datapoint for this print: \"Shares fell 3.3% after hours despite the beat.\" No closing-day move, no subsequent move, and no explanation of the decline appear in the note. Separately, screen data pulled 2026-09-04 shows a price of 369.83 USD, -38% from the 52 week high and -39% from the all time high, with a forward P/E of 30.6 against a 4 year median of 72.3; the note attributes the de-rating broadly to competition (\"The first credible competitors in twenty years arrived, and the multiple halved\") and does not tie it to this quarter's report. Whether the two \"vs\" figures in the earnings line (468 systems placed vs 395; EPS $2.80 vs $2.19) are year-over-year or sequential is never stated in the note, so I make no directional claim about placements over any specific period and do not treat the placements thesis killer as tested either way.

new_risks.risk: A 1 point tariff hit is embedded in full-year gross margin guidance. Within this note, tariffs are named nowhere in the bear case section (which covers competition and instrument pricing pressure) and nowhere in the thesis killers list (procedure growth under 10%, placements down two quarters, instrument pricing cuts on a call, price trigger $290). Whether the hit is new this quarter, its source, and whether it persists beyond 2026 are not stated.
new_risks.quote: gross margin 68 to 69% including a 1 point tariff hit

new_risks.risk: Full-year procedure growth is guided to a range topping out at 15.5%, below the 16% the quarter delivered. Decelerating procedure growth under competitive pressure is already the core of the note's stated bear case and its first thesis killer, so this is a risk the framework already names rather than a new one.
new_risks.quote: Even after the drop the stock is 30x, which prices in continued mid teens growth that competition will erode.

dodged.topic: Why the stock fell on a beat
dodged.reasoning: The note states the beat and the 3.3% after-hours decline in the same sentence and offers no explanation from the company or the analyst for the gap. This is an omission in a short summary note, not evidence that management was asked and declined to answer; the note contains no call content at all, so I cannot distinguish a dodge from a summarization choice.

dodged.topic: Instrument pricing and any concessions to hospitals
dodged.reasoning: The note makes instrument pricing central twice, in the bear case ($1,800 to $3,200 per procedure cost that hospitals will negotiate down) and as a named thesis killer (pricing cuts disclosed on a call), yet the Q2 paragraph carries no pricing commentary in either direction. Absence of pricing content in the note is not proof it was absent from the call.

dodged.topic: Competitive response to Hugo and Ottava
dodged.reasoning: The note establishes both competitors as the central overhang and cites a third party, Oppenheimer, on their weaknesses, but the earnings section itself relays nothing from the company on competitive wins, losses, or displacement. The only prior-quarter remark, that Q1 also beat with the same competition overhang, likewise reports no company commentary.

dodged.topic: Duration and source of the tariff hit
dodged.reasoning: The 1 point hit is quantified in the guidance line and then not developed anywhere else in the note, with no origin, no exposure detail, and no indication whether it recurs in 2027.

not_determinable: The comparison basis of the two 'vs' figures: '468 da Vinci systems placed vs 395' and 'non-GAAP EPS $2.80 vs $2.19'. The note never states whether the second number is the prior-year quarter or the prior sequential quarter, so no direction over a defined period can be asserted, and the year-over-year placements thesis killer cannot be scored.
Whether full-year guidance for procedure growth or gross margin was raised, cut, or maintained. The note contains no previously issued guidance range for either metric.

Any sequential comparison to Q1 2026. The note's entire prior-quarter content is the clause 'Q1 2026 also beat with the same competition overhang', with no Q1 revenue, procedures, placements, EPS, margin, or guidance, so no metric can be compared quarter over quarter and no claim about what is new versus the prior quarter can be supported.
Management tone, prepared remarks, Q&A content, or any direct quotation from the company. The note carries none.
Whether the 1 point tariff hit is new to this quarter's guidance or was already embedded in an earlier one.
The magnitude of the beat versus consensus. The note asserts a beat but gives no analyst estimates for revenue, EPS, or procedures.
Segment detail: Ion versus da Vinci contribution, instrument and accessory revenue versus systems revenue versus service, and geographic mix. None appear in the note.
Lease versus purchase mix on the 468 placements, and its effect on revenue recognition, despite the note describing the buy-or-lease model in its business description.

Any market reaction beyond the 3.3% after-hours move: no closing-day move, no move over the weeks since, and no attribution of the 2026-09-04 price of 369.83 to this print rather than to the broader competition overhang.
Capital return: buybacks, share count guidance, or use of the $8.6 billion cash and investments balance. The note gives a historical diluted share count table only.
Backlog, system utilization per installed base, or procedures per system, which would separate placement growth from usage growth.

Whether any position, entry price, or prior thesis log exists for this name. The note contains no journal, trade record, or position data; its Verdict section states only 'Buy now, September tranche. Buy zone $335 to $390. Conviction 4 of 5.'

read.standing_caveat: A research note is already a summary, so its silence is usually the author compressing rather than management evading. thesis.why_on_the_list: Compounder bucket, rank 67. Forward P/E 30.6 vs a 72.3 median, 39% off its high, while procedures grew 16% last quarter. The first credible competitors in twenty years arrived, and the multiple halved.
thesis.business_quality: Razor and blade model with 11,710 da Vinci systems installed, up 12%, and surgeons trained on it for a career. Gross margin around 68 to 70%. Cash and investments $8.6 billion, no debt. Competition: Medtronic's Hugo (approved late 2025) and Johnson & Johnson's Ottava (cleared for ten general surgery procedures). Oppenheimer notes workflow problems for Ottava and footprint constraints for Hugo.
thesis.verdict: Buy now, September tranche. Buy zone $335 to $390. Conviction 4 of 5.

logged.thesis: Procedures up 16%, placements up, multiple halved to 30.6x from a 72x median because Ottava and Hugo arrived. Razor and blade model with no debt.
logged.wrong_if: Procedure growth under 10%, placements down twice, or a close under $290.

risks.bear_case: For two decades the bull case rested on having no competitor; now there are two, one of them built into the operating table with half the footprint. Hospitals under budget pressure will use the alternatives to negotiate down the $1,800 to $3,200 per procedure instrument cost. Even after the drop the stock is 30x, which prices in continued mid teens growth that competition will erode.
killers: da Vinci procedure growth under 10%, system placements down year over year for two quarters, or instrument pricing cuts disclosed on a call

wrong_if.text: Procedure growth under 10%, placements down twice, or a close under $290.

multiples.label: Forward P/E
multiples.basis_note: The two sides are not the same multiple. The left is a forward P/E, the Street's estimate of next year's earnings. The median on the right is trailing: the price at each fiscal year end divided by that year's reported diluted EPS. Where earnings are expected to grow, forward is mechanically lower than trailing, so this column reads cheap by construction.

multiples.label: EV/EBITDA
multiples.basis_note: Both sides are trailing, so this comparison is like for like.

own_history.caveat: The median is taken at 4 fiscal year ends, so it is a 4-point median. That is a thin basis for 'cheap against its own history' and it says nothing about whether the old multiple was deserved.
own_history.basis_warning: Read the P/E row with care. Across the 136 names that carry both comparisons, 85% print a negative 'vs median' on forward P/E with a median of -29%, against 50% and 0.0% on EV/EBITDA where both sides are trailing. That gap is the basis mismatch, not 136 companies being cheap. It is also correlated with growth: faster-growing names look cheaper here (rank correlation -0.28 against revenue CAGR, versus -0.15 for EV/EBITDA), because their forward earnings are further above their trailing ones. The score weights the like-for-like EV/EBITDA comparison more heavily for exactly this reason.

drawdown.caveat: The all-time high is the highest closing price; the 52-week high is an intraday high. They are not on the same basis, and the drawdown from the all-time high is therefore understated.

price_basis.note: The drawdowns and the multiple-versus-median above were computed inside the price screen from its own last close, which is not quite the price shown at the top of this page: the two come from different passes of the pipeline and differ by a fraction of a percent. Neither is wrong; they are just not the same number.

peer_set.label: Healthcare
peer_set.caveat: Not enough names in its industry to compare against, so this is against 25 others in Healthcare. A sector holds businesses that are not really comparable, so read the percentile loosely.

peers.verdict: priced above where its quality sits
peers.reasoning: It is the dearest quartile on price and mid-pack on quality, 48 points apart the other way: it is priced above where its measured characteristics rank among its peers. Sometimes that is the market seeing something these measures do not; sometimes it is not.
peers.why: The own-history comparison above says nothing about whether the old multiple was deserved. This asks a different question: where does this name sit among its peers on price, and where does it sit among them on the things a price is supposed to reflect.

written_view.text: At $369.83 and 30.6x forward with EPS growing about 28% year over year in Q2, the PEG is close to 1. Three year view with 15% growth: bear 24x is about $390, flat; base 32x is about $520; bull 40x is about $650.

score.caveat: A percentile against 150 names on one date. It has not been backtested; see the positioning page for why not.
